evals.prompt: I coordinate volunteers at Second Chapter, an after-school reading program in Cleveland serving 300 kids at 6 library branches. We have about 120 volunteers: reading buddies (1:1 with kids, some sessions in a corner of the library without staff right there), event helpers for our spring book fair, and a couple of pro bono folks doing our website. We've never had written roles or a screening policy. Help me set this up properly.
evals.expected_output: Position descriptions for each role, a written risk-tiered screening policy (reading buddies as Tier 3), onboarding sequence, scheduling sized to volume, layered recognition and retention tracking, with a check of state law/insurer requirements.
assertions: Provides or outlines position descriptions for each role including duties, time commitment, screening tier and named supervisor

Assigns screening tiers by risk in a written policy: event helpers low-tier, and reading buddies with potentially unsupervised access to minors at the highest tier (background check, sex offender registry check, fingerprinting where required)
Tells the user to confirm current state law and insurer/funder requirements for background checks before finalizing the policy
Separates orientation from role-specific training and includes a handbook and first-shift buddy
Recommends a volunteer management system given ~120 volunteers with automated 24–48 hour reminders and a no-show protocol
Includes layered recognition (in-the-moment, milestones, annual event, meaningful-role) and tracking 90-day and 12-month retention

evals.prompt: volunteers keep ghosting after their first shift at our food bank. we get tons of signups from the corporate days. what's going on
evals.expected_output: Uses funnel data to locate the drop at the post-first-shift stage, diagnoses it as an onboarding/first-shift problem rather than recruitment, and recommends stage-specific fixes and tracking.
assertions: Recommends pulling funnel numbers (inquiries → applications → placements → active after 90 days) to locate where the drop concentrates
Identifies post-first-shift drop-off as an onboarding/first-shift experience problem rather than a recruitment problem
Recommends a first-shift buddy, clear role/orientation, and a 2-week check-in
Recommends automated reminders and a no-show protocol rather than assuming a motivation problem
Warns against defaulting to 'more recognition' or more recruitment as a blanket fix

evals.prompt: We need to show the board what our volunteers are worth. Last year they gave 18,400 hours. Also, we just realized our Tuesday senior-center visitors have been going into homes alone with no background checks for 2 years. Can you handle both?
evals.expected_output: Calculates volunteer value using the current published rate (to be looked up) paired with outcomes and a capacity argument, and immediately flags the screening gap as a risk issue requiring Tier 3 screening and risk-management review.
assertions: Tells the user to multiply hours by the current Independent Sector value-of-volunteer-time rate for their state and year (looked up at the source) rather than asserting a figure from memory
Pairs the dollar value with outcome stories and an FTE-equivalent capacity argument, warning that dollar value alone invites a 'replace them with money' misread
Immediately flags unsupervised in-home visits with vulnerable older adults and no background checks as a serious screening gap requiring Tier 3 screening
Recommends involving risk management/insurance review for the screening gap rather than waiting
Recommends documenting the tier in a written policy applied consistently

should_not_trigger.query: We need to recruit two new board members with finance and legal skills — how do we build a skills matrix?
